outline.unique_angle: Every competing page treats 'verify your AI output' as a one-line disclaimer. This piece shows the failure live with a dated, named clinical example (SABA-only vs AIR / GINA 2024) and converts it into a concrete, repeatable 4-step verification checklist a nurse can apply to any evergreen topic — grounded in a real first-person near-miss, which none of the top-3 offer.

warnings: AI Overview is present for the broad 'can you trust ai for medical advice' query and will steal clicks; only win by targeting the narrower long-tails and out-depthing on the concrete asthma example.

Top-3 is a mix of a thin (~600 word) nurse blog, an off-topic business cutoff post, and a high-DR academic study (DR 92) — the study is not directly competing on intent, so the realistic competition is the two DR 20-30 blogs. KD estimate band 9-18 is achievable for a new domain on the specific long-tails, less so on the head term.

YMYL topic: per project rules, requires RN byline, GINA 2024 + Australian Asthma Handbook citations, 'last reviewed' date, and 'in my practice / ask your supervisor' framing. Do not phrase as medical advice.

Clinical facts must be re-confirmed by fact-checker against the live GINA 2025/2024 strategy report and current National Asthma Council Australia handbook at write time — guidance keeps moving, which is the whole point of the article.
